subject: Post-call: EdgeFin performance SLOs & benchmark methodology (prompt sets + harness)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@edgefin.ai>, Priya Desai <priya@benchlabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: EdgeFin performance SLOs & benchmark methodology (prompt sets + harness)

Hi Alex / Priya 

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth:

Summary from today's discovery:
- Target 95th pctl latency <= 200ms for typical agent requests (avg output length ~150 tokens).
- Peak concurrency target: 320 concurrent streaming sessions during market open spikes.
- Sustained throughput requirement: ~1.2M tokens/day with burst capacity to 2x for peak hours.
- Streaming: client requires server-sent events (SSE) style tokens with latency per token <= 25ms p95 for interactive flows.

Benchmark methodology items we agreed to exchange:
1) Prompt sets: you (EdgeFin) will share representative prompts (incl. edge cases like large context, multi-turn state)  prefer JSONL labeled with expected output length.
2) Eval harness: Redwood will provide a reproducible runner (Dockerized) that measures cold/warm latencies, p50/p95/p99, token-per-second, and per-token emission latency for streaming.
3) Measurement definitions: we will use the attached measurement-defs.md as the canonical definitions (cold start = first token after model load, warm = subsequent request after KV warmup, concurrency tests inject KV cache warmup where applicable).
4) Reproducibility: seed files, model checkpoints, and run configs will be exchanged; harness will support tagging runs with HubSpot deal id (HS-12345).

Attachments included: edgefin_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (sample prompts), measurement-defs.md, redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.tar.gz (initial harness, README in root).

Proposed near-term next steps:
- Alex: send full prompt set + any custom tokenization notes by EOD Wed (10/14).
- Logan: we'll provision a dedicated benchmark node on a small Dedicated pool and share run commands.
- Priya: if you want to run your own independent lab runs, we can share the harness and help validate results.
- Rishi: I'll draft an updated mutual action plan that includes the benchmark acceptance criteria and timeline.

Please reply with any corrections. If everything looks good, Alex  can you confirm you'll share the prompt set by 10/14?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: EdgeFin performance SLOs & benchmark methodology (prompt sets + harness)

Marissa 

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming we will share the full prompt set by end of day Wednesday (10/14). Couple of clarifications before we hand it over:

1) There are two prompt families  web-chat (short interactive queries ~20-80 tokens) and analysis jobs (longer outputs ~400-600 tokens). For the analysis jobs we won't require streaming; the web-chat path needs streaming.
2) Tokenization: we use a custom tokenizer pre-tokenizer that approximates GPT-like token counts; I'll add a token_count field for each sample so your harness can compare apples-to-apples.
3) For concurrency, during market open we expect the majority (~70%) of sessions to be web-chat. We'll also provide a session distribution file.

I'll drop the prompt sets and a small doc outlining the session distribution into the Drive link you provided. Let me know if you prefer email attachment instead.

Best,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Engineering, EdgeFin
alex.turner@edgefin.ai

Awesome  thanks Alex. Couple implementation notes for the harness before you upload:
- Please include a "session_profile.json" that maps session types to probability weights (web-chat vs analysis). The harness will use that to generate realistic concurrent mixes.
- For streaming tests we'll measure two metrics: per-token emission latency (p50/p95) and time-to-first-token. Please mark any prompts that are multi-turn so we can exercise KV cache semantics.
- If you have any prompts that include large system/context (~8k tokens) mark them as heavy-context; we'll run a separate set of cold-start tests against those.

Logan & Rishi  can you take point on the provisioning? Logan, can we carve a 2-GPU Dedicated node (A100 equivalent, 80GB) for the initial runs? If not, we can do a hosted run with pinned capacity.

Thanks  talk soon.

Marissa

Marissa / team 

We can provision a 2x A100-80GB Dedicated node for initial runs next week. Notes/constraints:
- For streaming token latency measurements we need to ensure the runtime is pinned to a single model variant; multi-variant routing will skew p95. We'll run with the customer-picked quantization profile (please include in the run config).
- Concurrency load generator: the harness will simulate 320 concurrent long-lived SSE sessions (with heartbeat) and a separate burst generator for the analysis jobs to reach the 2x burst target.
- We'll run cold-start tests by restarting the model-serving process between runs; warm runs will execute 50 sequential requests to stabilize KV caches.

I'll upload the runner commands and SLURM-like run script into the Drive folder. Alex  quick ask: include a couple of ground-truth outputs for the analysis prompts so we can measure quality regressions in addition to raw latency.

Thanks,
Logan
